annotations.text:
A1 · A1-still-water
VOLUME: quiet  |  LIGHT: warm amber in blue

LAYOUT: ONE narrow centred column, no nav at all, huge air. Depth = 4 layers (ridge / figures / water / swan).

PHENOMENON: The surface is mirror-still until the cursor touches it, then the wake bends around the pointer — the water is listening. Reflected light continues past the video edge and moves across the type itself.

TRADEOFF: Weakest product proof of the eight — THE LOOP must sell charts in almost no room, and an impatient visitor gets no spectacle to remember.

REDUCED MOTION: Native. Remove cursor reactivity and the drift; a still frame with the amber reflection baked into the plate loses almost nothing — this is the only design whose fallback is nearly identical to the full version.

A2 · A2-dawn-approach
VOLUME: quiet  |  LIGHT: dawn

LAYOUT: Full-width alternating BANDS that warm as you descend; content zig-zags left/right. Sticky gradient progress bar. 5 depth layers.

PHENOMENON: The lake reflection is a live-inverted, blur-shifted duplicate of the video layer — the water responds to the footage with no second asset.

TRADEOFF: Weakest at trainer recruitment — the mood is so trainee-emotional that the business case lands late and soft.

REDUCED MOTION: The light progression becomes per-chapter static plates (night / warming / amber). The parallax silhouettes flatten to a single baked layer. Arc survives; motion does not.

B1 · B1-harbor-lights
VOLUME: people-first  |  LIGHT: dusk

LAYOUT: Left rail nav + a WALL of lit windows; the skyline IS the activity feed. 5 depth layers, 14 drawn figures.

PHENOMENON: Every lit window maps to a real workout logged on the platform tonight — the skyline's brightness IS the community's activity.

TRADEOFF: GLM's own warning, accepted: the activity-driven skyline goes dead-static at launch with no user data, and the warmth can bury the product's craft. Needs a designed empty state.

REDUCED MOTION: Swans land as a static populated composition rather than accumulating; windows use a fixed lit pattern rather than live activity.

B2 · B2-two-lanterns
VOLUME: people-first  |  LIGHT: cold crystalline, warm windows

LAYOUT: Strict THREE columns with a sticky 420px river of video down the middle and a door panel on each flank.

PHENOMENON: One video element is CSS-masked into three disjoint regions (hero river, mid-page slit, fork backdrop) so a single swan appears to swim continuously down the whole page.

TRADEOFF: Worst cinematic range — the rigid split-grid caps how big any single moment can get, and THE PROOF feels cramped. NOTE F7: the tall crop yields ~540px of real width; expect softness or substitute a generated plate.

REDUCED MOTION: The masked-swim illusion is the design; without motion the three regions become three still crops of the same frame, which still reads as one continuous river. Survives well.

C1 · C1-instrument-flight
VOLUME: product-forward  |  LIGHT: cold crystalline

LAYOUT: Nine/three split with a STICKY telemetry rail; the flight path IS the chart. Data reads as instruments.

PHENOMENON: Moving the cursor through the wake re-plots the trend line live, ice crystallising along the new curve.

TRADEOFF: Coldest read of the eight — 'homey' is at real risk and a non-technical trainee may feel lectured by instruments rather than welcomed.

REDUCED MOTION: The wake-chart renders as a finished static plot; the sticky rail becomes a normal column. Legible, but the central idea (the chart being DRAWN by flight) is lost — this design loses the most in fallback of the product-forward pair.

C2 · C2-the-instrument
VOLUME: product-forward  |  LIGHT: dusk

LAYOUT: Fifty/fifty SPLIT: the left half is fixed and never moves while the right half scrolls past it.

PHENOMENON: The chart's line is made of the same light as the water — data and world are one substance. The hero's telemetry and THE PROOF's charts are driven by ONE dataset, so the page's data feels continuous rather than decorative.

TRADEOFF: Most likely of the eight to convert a skeptical trainer and least likely to make anyone feel anything; risks becoming a SaaS page wearing a swan.

REDUCED MOTION: The chart appears already drawn, with the light-substance treatment baked in. Loses the reveal, keeps the idea — the strongest fallback of the product-forward pair.

D1 · D1-beneath-the-waterline
VOLUME: full-cinematic  |  LIGHT: deep night rising to dawn

LAYOUT: Full-bleed STRATA with depth markings (-12m ... -61m), diving through night and surfacing into dawn at the fork.

PHENOMENON: The waterline never leaves — surface light refracts down through every chapter, and a set logged in THE LOOP sends a ripple upward that crosses the hero's horizon.

TRADEOFF: The entire premise rests on desktop motion, and it needs the 23.976fps interpolation cost owned up front (F7).

REDUCED MOTION: GLM's own warning, accepted as a requirement: this must ship as a DIFFERENT, still-art-directed page — six full-bleed static plates, one per chapter, carrying the same night-to-dawn arc — not as a long dark scroll with the motion switched off.

D2 · D2-vegas-mile
VOLUME: full-cinematic  |  LIGHT: deep night neon

LAYOUT: Marquee bulb strip, neon signage blocks, wet-pavement reflections. The loudest of the eight.

PHENOMENON: Neon casts real-time blurred colour reflections onto a wet-pavement gradient layer that shifts with scroll velocity — the street feels rained-on.

TRADEOFF: Highest performance risk of the eight and the worst reduced-motion story; also the furthest from 'homey' — closest to Sean's stated Las Vegas reference but at the cost of warmth.

REDUCED MOTION: Kimi's own warning, accepted as a requirement: strip the scroll-binding and this collapses into the exact 14-equal-sections sin the run exists to cure. The fallback must be six deliberately different-sized static blocks, art-directed as a sequence, or this design is disqualified.

EIGHT DIRECTIONS — REFACTOR v2 (2026-08-19)

v1 was rejected: one template, eight colour swaps. The gate had measured the JSON skeletons, not the rendered pages.

WHAT CHANGED
• Eight INDEPENDENT layout functions — different nav, grid, hero, chapter arrangement.
• REAL parallax: CSS perspective + translateZ, 4-6 drawn depth layers per board. No stock plates.
• People are DRAWN into the world now, not asserted in a text field.
• SwanStudios is not only training: Dance, Art & Visual Expression, Vocal & Sound Work, Photography & Graphic Design, Community — copy verbatim from CreativeExpressionSection.tsx, which is BUILT but not mounted in HomePage.V4.

SHARED (never varies): the copy pack, the six chapters, two equal doors, the 15%/$1,000 economics, the H3 credit.

Gold tags = new copy needing Sean's approval.
